method: Only a fixed set of prose words glued to numeric values is split; code-like identifiers are excluded. Quotes, code, paths, citations, regex literals, ranges, hashes, versions and URLs are protected. After-comma spacing changes delimiters only. The citation and identifier inventories and every protected span are compared byte-for-byte.

behavioral_openings.first_sentence: The reusable retry loop always makes the initial assistant-producing call, then decides from its returned message whether another call is allowed.
Models separates synchronous last-known catalog reads from asynchronous credential-aware availability and refresh.
createProvider accepts either a single ProviderStreams object or a map of API names to implementations.
The request retry helper wraps an SDK call configured with maxRetries=0 so every retry is an independently cancellable request.
The ordered display/runtime levels are off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max and ultra.
buildBaseOptions combines model and request settings into the shared adapter envelope, with request sampling keys overriding model defaults.
isContextOverflow classifies the completed assistant message using both the normalized stop reason and provider evidence.
estimateContextTokens accepts either messages alone or a full Context and returns both the total estimate and its checkpoint/trailing components.
createAssistantMessageDiagnostic builds one diagnostic from an arbitrary thrown value and optional details.
normalizeProviderError extracts SDK-shaped status/body data and marks whether the original Error.message already carries the selected body.
parseStreamingJson tries complete JSON parsing before applying any repair.
The TS validator caches a compiled TypeBox validator by schema object identity in a WeakMap.
resolveJsonSchemaStrictSampling returns true for a supported strict request and undefined when strict is absent or unsupported in prefer mode.
transformMessages first normalizes nullish message content to an empty array and downgrades unsupported user/tool images to distinct omission placeholders.
TS has both a legacy image API registry and a provider-owned ImagesModels collection.
getProviderEnvValue checks an own property in the supplied environment first and falls back only when its value is undefined; an explicit empty string therefore remains meaningful.
The standalone TS AI-package CLI filters built-in providers to those declaring OAuth and exposes help, list and login.
The enable helper recognizes ICE_PROVIDER_CONTINUATION_DIAG values 0/false/off and 1/true/on; otherwise Vitest disables it and the exact provider ID codexlb is enabled by default.
Every provider-facing conversation consists of user, assistant and tool-result records with exact role tags and role-specific content.
The direct stream accepts AnthropicOptions, while streamSimple authenticates synchronously and builds the shared base envelope before selecting adaptive or budget-based thinking.
The adapter checks a provided key or nonempty authorization/x-api-key/cf-aig-authorization request header before constructing a client.
The TS decoder buffers UTF-8 text, accepts CR/LF line boundaries, joins multiple data fields with newlines and flushes a trailing frame at EOF.

The adapter projects messages, deduplicates active tools by normalized name using Map insertion order with last value winning, and separates immediate tools from tools first marked available before use.
The adapter resolves a concrete compatibility record before converting history, tools and request options.
The default request includes the complete locally converted input, stream=true and store=false.
TS extracts chatgpt_account_id from the token's https://api.openai.com/auth payload claim and sends an account-bound Codex request.
TS resolves the deployment separately from the logical model and uses an AzureOpenAI SDK client.
TS posts {model, context, options} to the model base URL plus /messages and optionally adds debug=1.
Bedrock requests use a fresh AWS SDK client with explicit endpoint and credential precedence.
The Bedrock adapter builds shared inference fields and Claude-specific thinking controls before sending a command.
Bedrock history conversion translates neutral messages into Converse content blocks and groups consecutive tool results.
The Bedrock stream mapper reconstructs indexed text, thinking and tool blocks from AWS events.
The Google adapter constructs a GoogleGenAI request and converts its stream into the common assistant events.
Vertex selects API-key authentication or application-default credentials before constructing its GoogleGenAI client.
Google thinking configuration depends on the model family and whether the caller uses direct or simple options.
Google history conversion preserves ordered multimodal content and attaches replay signatures only when identity and syntax checks permit them.
Google tool conversion uses full JSON Schema by default and supports a separate legacy parameter conversion.
Google and Vertex share a mapper that turns the first response candidate into consecutive assistant blocks.
The Mistral adapter uses the SDK chat-stream endpoint despite its historical API name.
Mistral history conversion assigns request-local tool IDs and reuses each mapping for calls and results.
The Mistral mapper assembles text, thinking and tool calls from the first streamed choice.
Retention resolves from an explicit truthy option, otherwise ICE_CACHE_RETENTION=long, otherwise short.
convertMessages first calls the shared cross-provider transform with a Chat Completions-specific tool-ID normalizer.
The TS adapter emits start only after the HTTP request and response hook succeed.
The shared TS processor maps output_index to independent thinking, text or tool slots.
The TS converter first normalizes the transcript through the shared transform, supplying a Responses-specific tool-ID callback.
TS tries a WebSocket for every transport value except sse, unless the session has a sticky SSE fallback marker.
TS serializes the final request body once and attempts synchronous zstd compression at level three when the runtime exposes it.
TS sends one nonstreaming chat-completions request containing a single user message of text/image parts.
The TypeScript generator combines remote model feeds with curated provider rules, producing typed provider catalogs and a hash-checked data manifest.
AgentMessage is the provider Message union plus every value of the declaration-mergeable CustomAgentMessages interface.
StreamFn may return an AssistantMessageEventStream immediately or a Promise of it.
The module owns one mutable defaultStreamFn.

runAgentLoop clones the context object and transcript array, initializes newMessages with the supplied prompts, emits agent_start then turn_start, emits start/end for each prompt, and enters the loop.
After initial events, poll steering once.
For each request pass the current AgentMessage array and signal to optional transformContext, await the returned array, then await convertToLlm on that result.
Call getApiKey with current model.provider on every request, await it, and use its value when truthy; undefined or empty string falls back to config.apiKey.
Await the stream factory.
In the done/error event branch, await response.result; if finalMessage.stopReason is exactly error and the run AbortSignal is already aborted, mutate it to aborted before message_end and turn_end.
Collect every assistant content block whose type is toolCall in source order.
Prepare calls serially in assistant order.
Find the first registry tool whose name exactly equals toolCall.name; missing returns Tool <name> not found with no hook.
prepareToolCall checks abort after an awaited before hook and again before returning prepared.
Each prepared execution creates acceptingUpdates=true and an array of sink promises.
Only a prepared/executed path reaches afterToolCall, including execute exceptions converted to an error and cancellation caught at the execute-entry guard.
createErrorToolResult produces exactly one text block and details={}, with no usage or terminate property.
For sequential or parallel finalized calls, terminate is true exactly when the list is nonempty and every final result.terminate===true.
After turn_end call prepareNextTurn with current assistant, ordered tool results, current context and all newMessages.
Invoke shouldStopAfterTurn after preparation and before steering/follow-up drains.

Initialize systemPrompt="", model=the exact unknown placeholder, thinkingLevel=off, tools/messages=[], streaming=false, no streaming/error message and an empty pending-tool Set, overridden by supplied initial configuration.
subscribe stores callbacks in a Set and returns a closure that removes that exact callback; there is no replay.
Use two independent FIFO arrays.
Reject an active run first and reject an empty transcript.
runWithLifecycle rejects reentrancy, creates one AbortController plus a completion promise, sets activeRun and streaming state before invoking the executor.

Construction and public fields accept convertToLlm, transformContext, streamFunction, getApiKey, onPayload/onResponse, beforeToolCall/afterToolCall, shouldStopAfterTurn, legacy prepareNextTurn(signal), context-aware prepareNextTurnWithContext(context, signal), sessionId, thinkingBudgets, transport(default auto), maxRetryDelayMs and toolExecution(default parallel).
prompt checks busy status before normalization.
Agent.abort aborts only the current controller and is a no-op while idle.
streamProxy returns a ProxyMessageEventStream immediately and launches one asynchronous request.
Use response.body.getReader and a streaming TextDecoder.
start returns the existing partial without resetting it.
Register an abort listener that calls reader.cancel("Request aborted by user") when a reader exists and swallows cancellation rejection.
AgentHarness.create simply constructs the object and returns {harness, suspended:[]}; it does not scan records, recover operations, validate model identities or start a loop.
PassiveRegistry implements both hooks.on and events.on by ignoring name/handler/options and returning an empty unsubscribe closure.

Construction keeps the supplied session/model by reference; sets thinking off; active tools to supplied activeToolNames, else every supplied tool name, else[]; copies tool/resource arrays; shallow-copies stream options; retains supplied retry/compaction objects or uses defaults.
name is always main.
Two modules define the same structural Result union.
ExecutionEnv is FileSystem+Shell.
NodeExecutionEnv.absolutePath calls resolvePath(cwd, input): exact ~ expands to homedir; ~/ and, only on Windows, ~\ expand via join(homedir, remainder).
Resolve the path, return an aborted FileError before I/O when signalled, then call readFile with encoding utf8 and the AbortSignal.
Resolve/precheck cancellation.
readBinaryFile resolves/prechecks then calls native readFile with signal and returns Uint8Array bytes without text decoding.
The FileSystem interface declares appendFile(path, content, abortSignal?), but NodeExecutionEnv implements only path/content.
fileInfo resolves the logical path and calls lstat.
Resolve/precheck cancellation, call readdir with dirents, then process entries serially in the returned order.
canonicalPath resolves the logical input then awaits realpath, returning the canonical path or a mapped FileError.
createDir resolves then mkdir({recursive:options.recursive??true}); remove resolves then rm({recursive:options.recursive??false, force:options.force??false}).
createTempDir defaults prefix tmp-, calls mkdtemp(join(os.tmpdir(), prefix)), and returns its path or a FileError without a target path.
On every exec call resolve shell configuration.
With inheritEnv omitted/true, build a new map by spreading process.env, then constructor shellEnv, then call env; later values win.
Precheck abort, validate timeout, choose cwd from a truthy call cwd resolved against environment cwd or use stored cwd, resolve the shell, then access cwd(F_OK).
setEncoding(utf8) on each child pipe maintains decoder state across chunks.
Undefined timeout means none.
waitForChildProcess listens for child error/exit/close and each pipe end/data event.
cleanup iterates the current activeChildPids Set, calls killProcessTree for each, then clears the Set.
Accept one path or an ordered path array.
Both TS resource modules duplicate the same frontmatter parser.
Prompt invocation substitutes an already supplied argument array into template text, while the separate argument lexer splits a raw command string.
loadSourcedPromptTemplates processes inputs {path, source} sequentially through loadPromptTemplates.
Accept a directory string or ordered array; explicit file inputs are ignored by this agent-package helper.
For each visited directory read the three names in that order using env.joinPath and fileInfo.
Read/parse the skill file.
loadSourcedSkills processes each {path, source} input in order through loadSkills.
BashExecutionMessage is a flat custom role with command/output/exitCode/cancelled/truncated/timestamp and optional fullOutputPath/excludeFromContext.
createBranchSummaryMessage stores summary/fromId; createCompactionSummaryMessage stores summary/tokensBefore; createCustomMessage stores customType/content/display/details.

TypeScript convertToLlm maps in original order: drop bashExecution when excludeFromContext is truthy, otherwise render it into one text block; convert custom string to one text block or reuse its content array, regardless of display; wrap branch/compaction summaries using the exact envelopes; pass user/assistant/toolResult objects through unchanged; drop every other role.
Validate the requested timeout before creating a process or adopting a background shell.
The tool builds a fresh spawn context per invocation and passes the rewritten context to its backend.
Explicit background mode transfers process cancellation ownership from the tool invocation to a session registry.
A foreground invocation registers a release closure and races its execution against that release promise.
The registry owns in-memory shell records and monotonic IDs for one session.
bash_output distinguishes listing, incremental output and full-log query modes.
The query path streams a bounded suffix of a stored log for grep and reads a bounded byte tail for plain tail requests.
The registry distinguishes a running shell, an ordinary finished shell and a finished shell with a still-live process group.
bash_input requires a known running shell with an open retained writable stream; it cannot attach stdin to an arbitrary process after launch.
OutputAccumulator consumes Buffer chunks and decodes display text with one streaming TextDecoder, preserving split UTF-8 code points.
One BashWatchRegistry subscribes to shell start, output and state changes, and owns watch IDs, timers and fire listeners for the session.
Pattern watches perform a case-sensitive literal substring search over a short carry plus each new decoded output chunk.
Time-based watches schedule against each shell's lastOutputAt rather than simply its adoption time.
The model-update path and TUI redraw path use separate throttles.
The harness captures a sanitized text stream through ExecutionEnv while maintaining a 100 KiB recent tail and global output statistics.
executeBashWithOperations feeds a streaming TextDecoder into stripAnsi, binary-control sanitation and CR removal before invoking onChunk.
execCommand spawns command with args, shell:false, the explicit cwd argument, ignored stdin and piped stdout/stderr.
The coding-agent factory switches over seven fixed built-ins and passes only that tool's options.
Head truncation preserves complete initial lines; tail truncation preserves complete final lines unless the final line alone exceeds the byte limit.

All coding-agent tool paths normalize a defined Unicode-space set, remove one leading @, expand only literal ~ or ~/ (also ~\ on Windows), decode file:// URLs, and resolve dot segments against normalized cwd.
The coding-agent queue separates admission from execution: a global registration promise serializes asynchronous canonical-key resolution, then each canonical path has its own promise gate.
Read first resolves the ordered path variants, checks readability, then branches on detected image MIME.
Image processing first validates magic bytes, then normalizes/converts the MIME and optionally resizes the decoded image.
The write tool resolves the destination and enters the canonical-path mutation queue before creating parents or writing.
prepareArguments normalizes legacy input before schema validation.
The edit definition computes a read-only preview only after arguments are complete and replaces it with the result's actual diff on settlement.
Each rich ToolDefinition supplies renderCall/renderResult functions and reusable state rather than relying only on a generic JSON viewer.
The default tool runs fd directly with a protected argv array, while custom FindOperations can supply the entire glob search.
The tool runs rg in JSON mode, collects match events up to a global limit, then formats output after the child exits so context reads may be asynchronous.
Resolve path||'.', check existence and directory status, fetch names, sort them, then stat each entry to choose its suffix.
takeOverStdout is idempotent and records the original stdout/stderr write methods before redirecting ordinary process.stdout.write to stderr.
Branch order determines where the stop boundary is first encountered.
Forking copies structural history into a fresh store and starts its accounting at zero.
These lists are projections of JavaScript Maps; creation order is observable and updating an existing key does not move it.
The TS adapter lists and opens sessions through a supplied repository, then scans all entries oldest first.
The repository lazily resolves one database path and memoizes one open connection; session metadata remains available through typed Session instances.
Each active session has a serialized operation queue and a renewable database lease identified by owner id and monotonically increasing fence.
TypeScript uses entries.parent_id as the canonical conversation tree and a session-wide monotonically increasing sequence shared across entries, records, lane moves and facts.
Canonical parent links remain in entries; the cache records their complete paths, including entries before old compactions.
The search adapter uses the same canonical database as the repository and lazily initializes FTS5 only for a nonblank query.
Both TypeScript implementations estimate roughly one token per four JavaScript UTF-16 code units, with a fixed image allowance.
The harness materializes retained messages into its checkpoint rather than referencing the old JSONL tree boundary.
Collection is separate from navigation and persistence.
Coding-agent defaults are enabled=true, thresholdPercent=85, reserveTokens=16384, keepRecentTokens=20000 and midRunCompaction='off'.
The wrapper first retries provider failures under the configured policy, then validates the final response.
The coding AgentSession evaluates automatic compaction before an idle prompt and during run settlement, and can compact between tool turns.
Manual compaction claims a session-wide lock synchronously before asynchronous work and exposes a settlement promise.
Automatic compaction shares the session lock but returns false immediately when another compaction or branch summary owns it.

The session applies a safety gate before the shared retry classifier: context overflow, a toolCall block in the failed assistant, or a possible tool effect in that assistant generation all prohibit an ordinary retry.
Prompt preflight is a staged operation before the agent run.
sendCustomMessage assigns role='custom', the caller's customType/content/display/details and a fresh timestamp; live content normalizes null/missing input to [].
AgentSessionRuntime guards access with availability and exposes a stable runtime_unavailable error during an invalid or failed replacement.
AgentSession's internal subscription survives removal of public subscribers and processes core events serially.
The session builds builtin definitions, then overlays registered extension definitions and finally SDK custom definitions by name.
executeBash checks a pre-aborted caller signal before acquiring work, then creates a controller in a session-owned Set and links only that operation's caller signal.
Each AgentSession owns one BashBackgroundRegistry and one BashWatchRegistry.
navigateTree first rejects a pre-aborted signal, active run or any compaction/branch summary; selecting the current leaf returns a no-op.
getSessionStats scans all SessionManager entries, including abandoned branches.
createAgentSession resolves cwd from explicit options, then the supplied SessionManager, then process.cwd; agentDir is explicit-resolved or the global config default.
Coding SessionManager writes a first parsed header {type:'session', version:3, id, timestamp, cwd, parentSession?}, where timestamp is ISO text and parentSession is a source file path.

loadEntriesFromFile normalizes the path, returns [] for absence, reads 1 MiB chunks with StringDecoder so UTF-8 boundaries are preserved, skips blank/malformed JSON lines and accepts a valid final line without a newline.
A new persistent SessionManager initially holds a header and metadata entries in memory.

findMostRecentSession considers .jsonl files with a valid bounded-discovery header, optionally requires a nonempty header cwd whose resolved path matches the requested cwd, and sorts by filesystem mtime descending.
branch validates the target, changes only the leaf pointer and emits leaf_changed only when it actually changes; resetLeaf behaves likewise.
getEntries returns a new array excluding headers but shares entry objects; getEntry/getHeader/getLeafEntry return the stored objects, and getChildren walks insertion order.

bindExtensions updates only binding fields explicitly provided, applies UI/mode and command context, replaces the prior error subscription, awaits the configured session_start event (startup by default), then runs resources_discover.
setModel awaits checkAuth and throws 'No API key for provider/id' on a falsy result, then assigns the model, appends model_change, saves default provider/model and reclamps the reasoning preference.

computeContextBreakdown uses ceil(JavaScript string length/4) and a fixed category order: systemPrompt, contextFiles, skills, tools, promptAdditions, conversation, toolResults, extensionMessages, summaries, shell.
exportToJsonl resolves an explicit path or a timestamped session-<ISO-with-colons/dots-replaced>.jsonl against process.cwd, creates parent directories and overwrites the target synchronously.
The configuration module derives identity from the packaged manifest and computes resource paths without opening user state.
The TypeScript helpers identify the running distribution before constructing argv, and the executable self-update path additionally checks ownership and writability.
Trust is a resource-loading decision computed before normal project resources are loaded.
The trust store is a flat JSON object keyed by canonical absolute directory paths.
Configuration strings are parsed as environment templates unless their first character is an exclamation mark, which selects the command path in SET-006.
Only a leading exclamation mark selects command execution, and the remainder is the exact command string.
The manager reads separate global and project JSON documents through a synchronous lock callback.
The manager keeps global, project and effective settings separately, including the provenance of explicitly configured leaves.
Settings writes carry a snapshot of both values and the top-level or nested fields changed by this manager.
Migration runs when file or in-memory settings are loaded and again when the latest file is read for a changed-field write.
These accessors read the effective settings snapshot but deliberately treat favorites as global user state.
The settings manager exposes compaction and retry policies from its merged snapshot, applying defaults at read time.
Timeout parsing accepts nonnegative finite numbers, numeric strings and case-insensitive 'disabled', then floors numeric values.
The timer getters share strict explicit-value timeout parsing, so zero disables a timer while an invalid supplied value raises a diagnostic.
Most display getters read the effective snapshot and default only their own key, while setters save global values through changed-key persistence.
The settings manager exposes two separate nested objects: images governs provider payload processing, while terminal governs display.
The theme getter and appearance getter deliberately use different scope rules.
The manager provides explicit accessors for update-related state and two independent data-sharing switches.
Resource getters return shallow copies of their effective arrays, and user/project setters store the chosen scope through the settings persistence path.
The ice namespace has a typed storage shape but is not validated by these accessors.
reload rebuilds resource collections after reloading settings for the current trust state.
The loader first forces projectTrusted=false and reloads settings so project packages/extensions cannot participate in their own trust decision.
SourceInfo records both a logical resource path and the metadata that explains why it was loaded.
Conflict detection walks the final extension order and remembers the first owner of each tool/flag name.
The loader chooses the first readable regular instruction file in each directory and places global instructions before root-to-working-directory instructions.
The loader resolves explicit prompt input or discovers a permitted configuration file, and records both the resulting text and any existing source path.
A truthy customPrompt replaces the default scaffold but still receives append text, context files, eligible skills and the working-directory line.
Prompt discovery reads direct Markdown children of each selected directory and preserves the discovery order used by the resource loader.
Expansion applies only to a leading slash command that exactly matches the first template name, otherwise preserving the original input.
The loader treats a directory containing a regular SKILL.md as a skill root and stops recursion there.
Skill metadata comes from frontmatter and the containing directory, with warnings for most invalid fields and rejection only when the description is missing or blank.
The resource loader compares a metadata signature of the last resolved skill paths with the previous signature and reloads only when it changes.
Theme discovery reads JSON files from the ordered resource paths and isolates each file's load failure as a warning.
Extensions execute trusted TypeScript factories that register capabilities against a fresh instance.
Approved historical Pi imports resolve to the same ICE module objects as their canonical names.
Cached loads reuse imported factory functions for one cwd while rerunning initialization for each session instance.
Discovery loads project, global, and configured extensions in a defined precedence sequence.
A package can declare extension, skill, prompt, and theme resources in its ICE manifest.
Factory initialization stages selected registrations until the factory succeeds.
Load-time console messages can be buffered with the originating extension path and flushed when a sink attaches.
Handlers can be added and removed dynamically without rewriting a currently captured handler array.
An extension receives one API whose session actions become available when the host binds the runtime.
Invalidation makes guarded APIs and contexts reject future access with the first stored cause.
Tool registration updates the extension's live descriptor map and asks the host to refresh its tool registry.
A registered tool executes with a fresh extension context and reports newly enabled tools when the active set only grows.
Commands preserve their exact names and resolve cross-extension collisions into deterministic invocation aliases.
Extension shortcuts respect reserved application actions and expose diagnostics for collisions.
Extensions declare boolean or string flags with optional typed defaults.
An extension can contribute a named settings section with items and an onChange callback.
Extensions share a named event bus for asynchronous cooperation.
Provider registration supports both compatibility configurations and native TypeScript Provider objects.
The base extension context exposes live queries and controls through guarded getters and methods.
Command handlers receive additional session-control methods beyond the base context.
The runner reports extension failures and measures selected prompt-blocking handlers after they settle.
Generic events await each subscribed handler in extension and registration order.
A message_end handler can replace the completed message while preserving its role.
A tool-call handler can mutate the input in place or return a blocking decision before execution.
Tool-result handlers share one shallow event copy and can return ordered patches to content, details, isError and usage.
User-shell routing lets an extension supply execution operations or a complete result for a user !/!!
Context handlers transform the messages sent toward a model without directly editing the durable transcript.
Before-provider-request handlers can replace the exact outgoing provider payload.
Before-provider-headers handlers edit one shared plain header record.
Before-agent-start handlers can supply run-local prompt replacements and custom messages.
Resource discovery collects extension-contributed skill, prompt, and theme paths.
Submitted-input handlers can transform text/images or consume the input before later prompt processing.
The native boundary must preserve event data and ownership in addition to event names.
Pre-trust handlers can return a three-way project trust decision before ordinary project resources are admitted.
An extension tool carries behavior and policy metadata beyond a JSON parameter schema.
Interactive tool rows can use independent call and result renderers supplied by the tool definition.
A custom message renderer is registered under an exact customType and is selected for displayed custom messages of that type.
Custom entries are persistent extension state records that remain hidden unless an exact customType renderer is available.
Each extension may install one Markdown transformer; all installed transformers then form an ordered display-only chain.
Dialog calls are asynchronous UI requests whose cancellation defaults are undefined for text/selection and false for confirmation.
notify delivers a UI message immediately and does not append an LLM message or durable session entry.
setStatus stores keyed footer text, while the working and hidden-thinking controls modify shared interactive presentation.
A widget is stored under a plugin-supplied key in one of two editor-adjacent containers.
Header and footer setters replace shared UI components rather than registering additional independent rows.
custom creates a focused UI interaction whose factory receives TUI, theme, keybindings and a completion callback.
onTerminalInput installs an interactive raw-input listener and returns an unsubscribe function.
Editor text setters and paste are different operations: setEditorText directly sets content, while pasteToEditor routes a bracketed-paste sequence through the editor's input handler.
addAutocompleteProvider records a provider factory and rebuilds the autocomplete chain.
The UI context exposes a live theme getter and separate enumeration/load/set operations.
setToolsExpanded chooses a full expand/collapse state for the transcript and requests a redraw.
sendMessage uses one typed custom-message shape with explicit triggerTurn and deliverAs options.
sendUserMessage accepts a string or a content array and converts it into text plus optional images for the ordinary session prompt path.
appendEntry stores a custom state record without sending it to the model, while name and label setters delegate to the current session manager.
Tool inventory and active-tool queries are different: getAllTools describes configured definitions, while getActiveTools returns the names currently selected for the agent.
The extension setModel action accepts a complete model object and returns a Promise<boolean>, while thinking-level get/set use the current session state.
ExtensionAPI.exec checks that its runtime is active and delegates to the shared direct-process helper.
An inline extension is either a factory function or metadata containing name, factory, optional hidden and optional priority.
Binary messages are assembled from a length header and the bytes that follow it.
The binary codec accepts a deliberately limited set of values and rejects ambiguous or excessive input.
Version one defines the exact messages a binary client and server may exchange.
The server converts internal model and transcript data into stable protocol records.
A binary connection must complete its version handshake before requests may run.
The server owns an explicit set of listeners and closes the resources it acquired.
Several client connections can share one acquired session runtime.
The Unix listener publishes a socket only after checking ownership and permissions.
The Unix transports copy and serialize outgoing bytes within a retained-byte budget.
Each binary connection attempt has its own identity and decoder.
The binary client matches each response to its request and applies authoritative snapshots before reporting success.
Consumers borrow independent session handles while the client tracks shared or exclusive ownership.
The remote transcript view combines an authoritative snapshot with transient streaming changes.
RemoteSession coordinates one selected session while borrowing a client that may serve other consumers.
The experimental parser separates its Unix transport options from legacy command arguments.
The coding-agent transport reads bounded JSON records and validates each command before dispatch.
Protocol output reserves bytes before joining an ordered write queue.
Admission keeps reads responsive while preserving the order of mutations and session transitions.
Every admitted request owns its cancellation signal and any deadline.
RPC startup binds the runtime and extension interfaces before declaring readiness.
Prompt responses acknowledge successful preflight separately from the model run.
Clients can discover supported commands, inspect current state and request bounded diagnostic views.
Model discovery uses cached metadata until an explicit refresh is requested.
History commands provide ordered session, tree and message views with explicit cursor rules.
Session-changing commands run through the shared transition coordinator.
Remote callers can run user Bash and inspect background shell activity without consuming the model's output cursor.
RPC exposes the parent-owned subagent bridge and approval decisions.
The headless extension bridge sends dialogs and text-based UI updates to the client.
The settings endpoint exposes configured values alongside effective values and their scope.
A settings update validates scope, trust and value before changing the selected setting.
Structured commands expose source identity, a form schema and a revision token.
The host client starts a child process and verifies its capability response before reporting readiness.
The child-process client gives each command one pending response owner and bounds retained requests.
The client validates a response's command and nested payload before resolving its request.
Event subscribers receive future notifications independently, while idle waiters and collectors own their cleanup.
Rust's TCP proxy and shared TUI projection are existing capabilities to preserve.
A theme file is validated before runtime construction, then every color variable is resolved and each foreground/background role is converted to an ANSI prefix.
Each asset supplies a filename-matching name, reusable variables, all 51 required semantic color roles and three export background roles.
Available names combine the built-in catalog, valid custom JSON files and registered runtime themes, while the current palette is shared through a global symbol.
Export helpers resolve a named theme's JSON independently of the live ANSI objects and convert palette indices into CSS colors.
Code highlighting uses highlight.js output converted from nested HTML spans to ANSI formatting.
The process-local preset initializes from environment, can be set explicitly and is read by sym(key).
A single theme name is fixed, while a setting with exactly one slash selects a light and a dark palette.
Starting a theme watch closes the old watcher/timer and watches the custom-theme directory for the active name's JSON file.
Validation produces a complete v2 appearance object together with path-specific issues.
The shared resolver builds color functions for a foreground/background role and resolves theme tokens dynamically through the live theme proxy.
Profiles are JSON files in the global agent directory's appearance-profiles subdirectory.
importBundle accepts a JSON string no larger than 256*1024 UTF-8 bytes and versions 1/2 only.
The library operates on <customThemesDir>/<name>.json and returns success/error objects for writes.
A ThemeDraftSession tracks selected name, staged entries and deleted original names.
The profile draft overlays a Map of staged content on the current disk name list and a Set of deleted names.
InteractiveAppearanceController captures a settings baseline and at most one preview.
The engine receives a plain source line and returns nonoverlapping spans indexed by JavaScript code-unit offsets.
ThinkingVerbSelector cycles through configured words with a resettable index or chooses using an injectable random-number function.
The constructor snapshots the session appearance and selected theme, builds a root SettingsList with at most 20 visible items and search enabled, and owns an AppearancePreviewComponent.
The shared color screen stages a local color until Accept; cancel discards it.
The screen groups tokens into Core, Messages, Tools, Markdown, Diff, Syntax and Thinking levels, with a separate variable screen.
Profile Save uses a trimmed name or default-profile, optional description limited to 200 characters, an include-theme flag and either all appearance or selected sections.
Scenes are all, conversation, markdown, tools, input, chrome, footer; all is default.
effectiveAppearance falls back to built-in defaults before controller construction.
The component builds the complete settings list from a runtime snapshot and terminal capabilities, then delegates search/navigation to SettingsList.
ThemeSubmenu retains the original setting, edits fixed or automatic choices locally, previews cursor movement, and returns a selected setting only on Apply.
The component retains original text separately from formatted display text, builds a background Box around Markdown and applies appearance styling without mutating the prompt.
updateContent retains the last message and streaming flag, rebuilds text/thinking children in content order, and appends stop notices according to whether tool calls are present.
A custom renderer gets first opportunity to produce the message component; the default card is used only when it returns no component or throws.
Each wrapper uses Box(1,1, customMessageBg), starts collapsed and rebuilds its contents on expansion or invalidation.
The component resolves the built-in tool definition for its cwd, then independently prefers the registered definition's renderCall, renderResult and renderShell properties.
Compact rendering separates a title from indented result rows and chooses preview content by a strict state/tool precedence.
createToolComponent groups a call only when tool style is compact, describeExploration returns a description, and the component does not render its own shell.
The interactive composition root enables tool-toggle links only for fullscreen mode and supplies the fullscreen renderer an internal-action predicate plus URL callback.
The TS component creates a leading spacer, dim-or-Bash-colored dynamic borders, a command header and an animated Running loader with the current cancel-key hint.
renderDiff parses numbered changed/context rows and coalesces consecutive removals followed by additions.
FooterDataProvider discovers Git metadata from its cwd and caches branch/status values separately.

FooterComponent receives a session and read-only data provider and computes its projection fresh on every render; invalidate and dispose are compatibility no-ops because the provider owns caching/watchers.
Compact footer builds left/right StatusSegment arrays, assigns priorities and delegates width allocation to layoutStatusLine.
SessionHeaderComponent obtains fresh SessionHeaderData on every render and chooses a fixed ASCII or block mascot according to the symbol preset.
StatusIndicator extends the terminal Loader, carries kind working/retry/compaction/branchSummary and disposes by stopping it.
BorderedLoader chooses CancellableLoader by default or a plain Loader when cancellable=false, then builds top border, loader, optional spacer/cancel hint, final spacer and bottom border.
formatRunSummary combines the runDone symbol, supplied verb, formatShellRuntime(durationMs), separator symbol and endedAt.toLocaleTimeString with numeric hour/two-digit minute.
The component builds its border/title/search/list/details/hints synchronously from getAvailableSnapshot, requests a render, then begins a 15,000 ms refresh.
EnabledIds is null for all models or an explicit ordered string array.
Each AuthSelectorProvider carries id, name, authType oauth|api_key, optional method metadata and configured status.
LoginDialogComponent is a bordered Container with an overrideable provider/title, dynamic content and a reusable Input.
KEYBINDINGS spreads TUI_KEYBINDINGS and adds 68 app actions; module augmentation exposes those IDs to generic keybinding consumers.
Input routing first offers the raw packet to the extension shortcut callback.

editInExternalEditor creates a private mkdtemp directory under tmpdir with prefix ice-editor-, writes prompt.md as UTF-8, splits the supplied command on literal spaces and passes the temporary path after those arguments.
ShortcutsViewComponent removes empty sections and builds a title, section columns and footer.

Notice records carry id, four kinds, twelve ordered categories (extensions, mcp, tools, skills, prompts, themes, compaction, subagents, model, session, console, updates), source/title/detail, sticky/quiet/group flags, createdAt/updatedAt and count.

The event reducer ignores successful tools and creates quiet tool failures keyed by call id with JSON arguments and text output; MCP names match a nonletter-bounded case-insensitive mcp, then exact agent/subagent classify children.
The panel starts on Problems when any nonquiet warning/error exists; Problems itself includes quiet errors/warnings.
The panel subscribes to registry changes with one 100 ms coalescing timer and a 1 s runtime ticker (disableable for tests).

TranscriptDocument flattens only its designated chat container's direct children while rendering the document once; direct UserMessageComponent children record their starting rendered row and raw message text.

NewMessagesPill snapshots the message-array length on the first visible render away from the end, resets on transcript-id change or shrinking message count, and clears its snapshot while hidden or following.
The view holds a supplied breakdown snapshot and model label.
The component obtains getProjectTrustOptions(cwd), starts on the first option whose savedPath and trusted value exactly match the saved decision, or index 0.
The snapshot includes all non-parent views.
The list preserves caller order, starts at the requested entry ID or the last message, and renders ten centered items.
The searchable text concatenates id, optional name, allMessagesText and cwd; path is not included.
The three-row header shows current/all-project scope, threaded/recent/Fuzzy ordering, named/all filtering, progress/status and action/query hints.
Construction immediately loads current scope.

The list flattens supplied SessionTreeNode roots using iterative traversal, prioritizes children/roots whose subtree contains the current leaf, records assistant tool-call metadata and marks the active ancestor path.
Rows use a fixed two-cell cursor gutter, three-cell indentation steps, connectors/fold symbols, active-path bullet, optional warning-colored label and local-time label timestamp.
The host obtains the current tree/leaf and configured filter, rejects an empty tree and treats selecting the current leaf as a no-op status.
Users can inspect extensions, skills, prompts and themes by their source package or directory.
The picker saves resource choices directly through SettingsManager.
The dialog has a theme step followed by an analytics step.
The Armin command adds a monochrome animated portrait, while selecting the matching OpenCode Kimi model adds the color Daxnuts portrait.
Startup computes release notes before mounting the interactive interface.
A selector displays every option in a nonshrinking list and starts at the first index.
Submission trims the draft and routes built-in commands before normal prompts.
Rebinding captures the current runtime session before awaiting extension setup.
The clear action first clears a draft and a second invocation strictly within 500 ms requests shutdown.
The startup check runs only when TMUX is truthy.
The share command first checks gh authentication synchronously and exports the session to a fixed session.html in the operating-system temporary directory.
The renderer factory chooses a main-screen or alternate-screen implementation and enables application tool-toggle links only for fullscreen.
Clipboard paste tries an image before plain text.
Export and import share a small first-argument parser.
An empty /name request shows the current name when one exists and otherwise displays usage guidance.
The command lowercases its already-trimmed argument.
The debug callback renders the current UI at the terminal's column count and records the terminal geometry and timestamp.
TS shares Intl.Segmenter instances for grapheme and word segmentation.
TS extractAnsiCode recognizes CSI by scanning to m/G/K/H/J, OSC by BEL/ST, and APC by BEL/ST; unrecognized/incomplete sequences return null.
truncateToWidth returns empty at maxWidth<=0, optionally pads empty/short input, and returns original input if it fits even when the ellipsis itself is wider than the target.
TS recognizes OSC8 open/close with arbitrary parameter text, URL following the second semicolon, and either BEL or ST terminator.
Text defaults text='', paddingX=1, paddingY=1, optional custom background.
TS uses Shift=1, Alt=2, Ctrl=4, Super=8 and masks CapsLock64/NumLock128.
StdinBuffer emits individual data sequences immediately and retains incomplete CSI/OSC/DCS/APC/SS3/meta sequences behind a resettable 10 ms default timer.
TS starts raw UTF-8 stdin, enables bracketed paste, installs resize before Unix self-SIGWINCH, and enables Windows VT input after raw-mode setup.

TS drainInput(maxMs=1000, idleMs=50) pops pushed/active Kitty first, disables modifyOtherKeys, clears negotiation fragments, temporarily removes the component input handler while stdin continues consuming, and exits at max or an idle interval; finally restores the previous handler.
TS accepts arbitrary definition maps with defaultKeys:string|string[] and optional descriptions; declaration merging extends the typed Keybindings interface.

Stack stores component entries in order; addChild normalizes finite numeric gap/grow/shrink/min/max to nonnegative floored integers (fallback gap/grow/min 0, shrink 1, max MAX_SAFE_INTEGER), while basis is retained and normalized by allocation.
The symbol-based layout hook lets any component return vstack/hstack/scroll structure.
ScrollView owns exactly one child; unsupported nonvertical axis throws and add/remove/clear throw explicit errors.
Hidden never shows; Always shows for a positive viewport and reserves one column only if width>1; Auto appears transiently only when content overflows and user scrolling marks activity.
compositeTuiLine immediately preserves an image-bearing base row.
TuiBase starts with stopped=false/running=false.

Input order is pending OSC11 reply, color-scheme report, registered input listeners in insertion order, cell-size response, debug Ctrl+Shift+D, focus visibility/restore maintenance, then the focused component.
showOverlay captures preFocus, assigns a monotonically increasing focusOrder and appends membership.
Margins may be one number or four edges, each clamped nonnegative.
OSC11 must be exactly ESC]11;body followed by BEL or ST.
The renderer tracks previous lines/dimensions, logical content end, actual hardware row, viewport top and maximum rows rendered.
Without explicit layout root, TuiAltScreen wraps normal children in an implicit primary ScrollView with follow=end.
The viewport input listener consumes focus-in/out, wheel, SGR mouse and otherwise recognized mouse sequences before focused components.
Primary press records a point in deepest scroll content when there is no overlay, otherwise screen coordinates, and captures OSC8 URL from the displayed row.
Cell dimensions default to 9x18 pixels and are set/get without validation; the capability cache is lazy and reset makes the next get redetect.
isImageLine recognizes Kitty APC and iTerm2 File OSC anywhere in a line regardless of detected support, including large prefixed payloads.
A global insertion-ordered map stores imageId, columns, rows, pixel width/height with an increasing transmissionGeneration.

Size fitting floors and clamps maxWidthCells and optional maxHeightCells to at least 1, clamps image pixel dimensions to 1, computes min(widthScale, heightScale), allows upscaling, and ceil/clamps resulting columns and rows.
Constructor stores base64, MIME, theme, options and explicit dimensions or header result, falling back to 800x600.
Loader extends Text with horizontal padding 1, vertical 0 and prepends one blank line.
Each CancellableLoader owns one AbortController for its lifetime.
flash(message, duration=1000) assigns an increasing ID, schedules a timeout at max(0, duration), unrefs it, appends the entry and requests render.

Backward slices text before the UTF16 cursor, segments with Intl.Segmenter or a supplied segment callback, skips trailing whitespace unless atomic, then consumes exactly one atomic segment, one word-like segment up to its last ASCII punctuation boundary, or a contiguous nonword/nonwhitespace run.
KillRing ignores empty text; every nonaccumulating push adds an entry even if equal to the latest.
Case-fold both strings; empty query matches score 0 and longer query fails.
setValue preserves/clamps existing cursor; a separate setValueAndMoveCursorToEnd places it at end; neither resets history/action state.
The fixed prompt is '> ' and availableWidth=width-2; nonpositive width still returns that prompt.

Provider receives lines, cursorLine, cursorCol plus mandatory AbortSignal and optional force, returns a Promise of {items, prefix} or null, exposes optional triggerCharacters/shouldTriggerFileCompletion and owns applyCompletion.
Token delimiters are space, tab, double/single quote, equals.
Absent fdPath or pre-aborted signal returns[].
Clone lines, retain same cursorLine, replace current prefix-length span before cursor and keep suffix.
State contains at least one logical line and UTF16 cursorLine/cursorCol.
The editor buffers bracketed-paste chunks until ESC[201~, handles trailing input recursively and routes completed text through handlePaste.
Only regex-shaped markers whose ID exists in the paste registry are atomic.
Undo snapshots deep-clone state, paste map and counter.
addToHistory trims, ignores empty/consecutive duplicates, prepends newest and caps 100; submission itself does not append.

Priority is disabled-completion cleanup, pending jump, bracketed paste, parent copy passthrough, undo, open completion menu, Tab completion, deletion/kill/yank/navigation and newline/submit, then printable decoding.
Left/right and backspace/forward delete use Intl grapheme segments merged with owned paste markers, cross logical newline boundaries and keep cursor at the segment start/end.

A kill captures an undo snapshot and prepends backward or appends forward deleted content to the current ring entry only when the prior action was kill; unrelated typing/navigation/replacement breaks accumulation.
wordWrapLine returns text plus UTF16 startIndex/endIndex for each chunk, preserving source whitespace and all original content.
Decoration callback receives each logical line; exceptions become an empty list.
Normalize padding to finite floor>=0 and autocomplete visible rows to finite floor 3..20(default 5).
Build visual rows from the same concealed/wrapped presentation used to render.
Either jump binding enters direction mode.
Provider replacement cancels prior work; default triggers @/# combine with unique provider single-code-unit nonwhitespace triggers except slash.
Constructor retains item references and initial filtered list.
Display label when truthy else value.
Optional enableSearch(defaultfalse) creates Input.
Active submenu renders at full requested width with no parent chrome.
Constructor copies options and retains theme/default style.
Strict strike accepts exactly paired double tildes with nonspace/non-tilde boundaries and escaped content; single tilde remains literal.
Token hierarchy drives lists, quotes and block spacing.
Only inspect the final token, recursively following the final list item or blockquote; if it is code, extract an opening backtick/tilde run of length>=3 from raw token start.
For N header columns reserve 3N+1 border/padding cells.
Per-instance tableStyle wins over process default(initial'unicode').
Each image redraw parses placement metadata for every screen line.
chromeBorderGlyphs returns one of 11 families or null for none/unrecognized input.
The native parser treats the frontmatter name as identity, independent of the filename, and validates a strict schema before creating a frozen definition.
Compatibility parsing maps recognized Claude fields into the native definition schema and records warnings for discarded fields.
Discovery walks bounded directories and deduplicates physical Markdown files before applying name precedence.
Built-ins are ordinary lowest-precedence definitions with stable source hashes and no child-spawn names.
The V2 resolver validates global and trusted-project scopes independently, then composes a typed result with diagnostics and deprecation notices.
The evaluator combines all matching rules using deny before ask before allow, then applies opaque-command and mode ceilings.
Derivation starts from the class-specific child ceiling, applies an eligible raiser, narrows by child rules and agent mode, and finally intersects the parent decision.
The broker owns pending approval identity and settlement, while callers own the policy decision and applying an offered session rule.
Startup argument normalization rejects ambiguous or noninteractive sub-yolo configurations before the subagent extension can use the grant.
Hook configuration is strict data; executable handlers are registered separately under an owner object.
The dispatcher serializes eligible hooks and keeps denial sticky: later hooks receive skipped-deny records without executing.
Command policy is host configuration rather than an agent-supplied command string.
Each child has a durable lifetime ID and a deeply frozen version 2 contract.
Adapter registration is an explicit host assertion of independent child-safe execution, not a tool-description heuristic.
V2 binds exactly the frozen tool names and wraps each in the current permission guard before recording dispatch observations.
The registry is the lifecycle owner; UI/RPC only project records.
Completion identity is childID:completed-turn-count and the completion record is durable before delivery.
Launch freezes a complete contract for each fresh child, checks the whole batch before acceptance, and retains names for the parent lineage.
The live guard checks cancellation, budget and authority before executing each tool.
A parent owner has a configurable admission pool.
ChildTurnBudget wraps the existing session stream/stop/tool hooks rather than adding a second loop.

Revival reopens the child's durable transcript and frozen contract, checks ownership/hash/current authority and worktree existence/ownership, resolves the frozen model, and only then attaches a resident session.

The tool validates the strict task schema and resume exclusions, normalizes every context packet, resolves references, launches fresh children, then dispatches fresh and resumed turns in original task order.
agent_control resolves ids in preference to id and checks supplied references even for actions that later use the whole list.
Resource resolution records source and canonical path plus content hash during preflight, and revalidates those fields before session creation/revival and current-authority dispatch.
V2 selects structured_report when the task has outputSchema, any acceptance criteria, or agent name exactly review; otherwise plain_final_turn stays explicitly unverified.
Each run creates a fresh V2ResultObservations object.
The store redacts captured output, keeps a bounded inline prefix, and writes larger output behind an owner-scoped UUID.
The assurance library is pure and performs no I/O.
The Git wrapper uses literal execFileSync argv with a 60 s timeout, ordinarily9MiB maxBuffer and a larger260MiB cat-file bound.
Place patch artifacts outside both parent and child worktrees and reject symlink components.
Runtime apply requires a trusted parent in build mode, active agent_patch, an open patch and explicit allow for every affected parent write; ask is not silently approved.
The ice agents dispatch runs before normal startup and supports list [--json], validate [paths...] and prune [--apply] [--json]; unknown command/options return exit 2.

createIceSubagents builds a hidden inline ice-subagents extension at before-user priority, attaches an IceAgentViewBridge and exposes attach, overview and respondToApproval; subscriptions are available through the bridge.
The inline ice-subagents extension registers agent, agent_control and agent_patch; patch execution is sequential.
IceAgentViewBridge distinguishes parent, live subagent and historical-subagent descriptors, with mirror and controlled modes.
HubSource supplies rows, capacity, approvals, selected-child details, focus/stop/resume/delete/respond and subscriptions.
The pre-startup --import-agent-pack flag accepts one nonempty path in separate or equals form; a resolved value beginning with a dash is not accepted in either form.
buildSubagentTaskContract takes a separate nonblank objective plus strict optional kind, deliverable, constraints, nonGoals, knownFacts and verification.
This exported bootstrap library has no active V2 production caller in the audited src inventory.
snapshotIceSubagentRoute stores provider, modelId and SHA of capability fields (API, base URL, reasoning/thinking mapping, input modalities, context window and max tokens), without credentials.
deriveSubagentPromptCacheKey returns a key only for fork context.

Normalize at most 8 requirements with nonblank values<=512 characters, ID<=64 characters using the allowed alphanumeric/dot/underscore/hyphen form, kind command|path|env-present and required default true unless explicitly false.
Activity digests pick a path from path, file_path, filePath, root, cwd, display only lexically scoped paths and use redacted compact action text.
The launcher normalizes unsafe subagent flags first, then validates ICE flags, and on either error writes the error message to stderr and exits 1.
Run git rev-parse --show-toplevel at ctx.cwd.
Append the complete state with appendEntry("ice-safe-verify-state", state) at each persistence boundary.
Start with the exact PLAN_TOOLS or BUILD_TOOLS arrays below.
Require a nonempty string path, then resolve it lexically against ctx.cwd.
/plan toggles mode.
Canonical reference is provider + "/" + id.

before_agent_start emits one hidden message: plan mode gets ice-plan-mode-context with PLAN_MODE_PROMPT; approved build gets ice-approved-plan-context with APPROVED_PLAN_PROMPT; other build state emits none.
Reject execution outside initialized plan with isError=true.
Require initialized plan mode.
Require initialized plan mode.
Only initialized plan+pending+hasUI with nonempty Markdown opens selector "Plan mode - next step" with the exact four options below and {content:planMarkdown}.
Hide read_plan entirely while plan.status=none.
Run only in build with approved plan, policy fresh and defined contextCutoffAt.
After mode becomes build, compact policy invokes ctx.compact with the exact custom instructions below.
At agent_start clear last-turn tool/decision flags, scheduled flag and aborted flag.
After active-tool admission, approved-plan read gate and path check, add toolCallId to an in-memory Set for edit/write/legacy patch integration/agent_patch apply.
Require a consumed authorized ID and isError=false as in SAFE-017.
undefined or boolean false disables verification; any other non-string value errors.
Defaults: timeout 120000 ms, combined retained output 65536 bytes, termination grace 5000 ms.
verify returns undefined if no state or another run is active.
Register on the shared extension event-bus object at Symbol.for("ice.goals.host.v1") using Object.defineProperty(value=controller, configurable=true).
Require goalHostActive, initialized state, nonempty activeSessionId and activeSessionManager.

Validate native session identity first, then initialized build mode, trusted project, saved session (session file is not undefined), configured argv, neither request nor context signal pre-aborted, approved-plan read acknowledgement when applicable, and no verifierRunning or activeGoalVerification.

After applying tools and persisting on restore/mode change, call optional onCapabilityChange with Object.freeze({mode, tools:Object.freeze([...effectiveTools(ctx)]), bashEnabledInRecordedProcess, allowExternal:effectiveExternal}) and ctx.
The /ice-status handler is a no-op before state exists.
An explicitly defined `ICE_TELEMETRY` value overrides the saved setting; otherwise install telemetry defaults to enabled.
TypeScript records elapsed wall-clock milliseconds only when `ICE_TIMING` equals `1` at module evaluation.
The CLI first opens `observability.sqlite` under its resolved agent directory and attaches one recorder to the runtime session.
Starting a recorder creates a new run ID from the session ID, current epoch milliseconds and a random UUID, then builds an empty live ring and a main-thread summary.
User message starts become either a normal message row or a skill row when the skill-envelope parser recognizes an invocation.
A tool start allocates a running item; progress and completion search backward for the newest retained item whose threadKind is main with the same toolCallId and mutate it in place.
Lifecycle events become separate timeline items rather than one mutable lifecycle row.
A nonterminal memory observation is kept in a pending map by requestId; a succeeded/failed observation patches that item when the matching request is still pending.
Appended custom session entries carrying goal or verifier state are projected into goal activities.
A child lifecycle record emits activity only when state, last-turn outcome or patch state changes its deduplication summary.
Opening a store creates a dedicated schema and returns a synchronous persistence sink.
The store redacts individual string values during JSON serialization so it does not corrupt the outer JSON structure.
Replay is an ordered fold of persisted events, with separate APIs for listing runs and paging events.
Every request first passes a loopback Host check and then presents a matching token through the printed URL, Bearer header or cookie.
The server routes authenticated read requests to snapshots or stored replay and opens a live SSE stream with an initial snapshot.
One server merges its in-memory recorder with recently active persisted runs and polls foreign run events while clients are connected.
createObserveCogneeSource creates a lazy source object whose concurrent first calls share one connection promise.
The source caches the summary promise for 30 seconds from creation, including both pending and fulfilled values and coalesces graph requests only while a request is pending.
Knowledge routes validate method, decoded path structure and bounded JSON inputs before forwarding to the source.
The browser stores at most 500 activity rows keyed by run and item identity, updates existing rows in place, and coalesces paint work into animation frames.
Selecting an activity opens a structured inspector while preserving its scroll/disclosure state during repeated updates.
The pulse groups retained activities into 42 epoch-aligned time bins and weights different event kinds to show useful activity density.
The client keeps one EventSource connected while changing the visible run through snapshot requests.
The browser lazily initializes the Knowledge view and coalesces overlapping dataset refreshes.
The Knowledge view progressively previews visible documents and guards full-content/query rendering with a request counter.
The dataset table fetches the summary endpoint on first use and reuses its client-side summary until explicitly forced.
The graph client caches one settled graph for its selected dataset and coalesces overlapping loads for that dataset.
The browser runs a cooling force simulation using Barnes–Hut repulsion, degree-weighted springs and a weak centering force.
Graph interaction uses run-local browser state and read-only node selection.
Normalize the supplied environment, treat any nonnull object (including an array) as a possible stored configuration, then overlay accepted environment values over stored values over defaults.
Parse trimmed nonempty noncomment lines; remove an exact export-space prefix, split at the first equals sign, trim key/value, and remove one matching outer quote pair.
readCachedCogneeApiKey accepts nonempty trimmed api_key from object JSON.
findGitRoot starts at path.resolve(cwd), checks for any existing .git path while walking at most 24 directories upward, and returns the initial resolved cwd when no match.
Trim the host ID, replace runs outside A–Z/a–z/0–9/dot/underscore/hyphen with underscore, and keep at most 120 characters.
loadIceCogneeConfig catches file-read/JSON errors and validates undefined/default configuration; validation errors propagate to loadCogneeConnection.
Apply exactly the two shared credential regexes below, then slice to maxChars UTF-16 units; nonpositive limit returns empty.
truncateForCapture uses a string as-is, else JSON.stringify and catches serialization exceptions with String(value).
Append the endpoint path to the existing base URL pathname after removing one trailing slash, clear search/hash, and preserve the URL origin/path prefix.
Create a private abort signal with budget max(1, timeoutMs), absolute Date.now deadline and timer.
Normal reads validate Content-Length as only decimal digits and a safe integer; a declared over-limit body fails before acquiring a reader.
Accept a top-level array or object.results ??
Only for HTTP 404, read bounded JSON up to 4096 bytes under the same deadline and return true when object.error exactly equals Recall prerequisites not met.
POST the exact body below.
Build multipart fields datasetName, node_set, run_in_background="true", optional truthy session_id, and a text/plain Blob named ice-cognee.txt in field data.

POST camelCase datasetName, optional nonempty sessionIds array and runInBackground:true.
POST agent_session_name, type:"api", memory_mode:"hybrid", source:"api" and optional truthy session_id/nonempty dataset_names.
POST only agent_session_name with default timeout 15000 ms.
GET /api/v1/settings, default 5000 ms and 65536 transport bytes.

GET /api/v1/datasets with 1048576-byte cap and normal browse timeout.
Validate dataset UUID, GET /api/v1/datasets/<id>/data with 8388608-byte cap.

Validate both dataset/data UUIDs before fetch.
POST searchType, datasets:[dataset], query, topK default 10 and onlyContext:true to /api/v1/search.
Project only valid nodes with nonempty ID and the exact supported label/type/text/set fields below.
Validate dataset UUID; GET the singular /api/v1/datasets/<id>/graph path, not /graphs.
GET /api/v1/sessions?range=all&limit=<options.limit or 500> under the common 15000 ms timeout and 2097152-byte cap.
Require SESSION_ID_RE before request, URL-encode ID and GET /api/v1/sessions/<id> with 4194304-byte cap.
Each extension instance holds independent recallCircuit and rememberCircuit, initially failures=0/openUntil=0.

createPendingRemember computes SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 text, sets operationId to createdAt-hashPrefix16, and records dataset, nodeSet, createdAt, state=pending and full redacted caller-provided text.
Create and chmod the pending directory 0700; enumerate it.
readPendingRemember returns [] on directory-read failure, sorts .json filenames lexically, parses each independently and retains only records passing the exact shallow checks below.
Return without work when shuttingDown, disabled or no client.
bufferWarmup requires the runtime current sessionId, creates warmup/, counts .json files and silently drops a new entry at 256 files.
A dream record stores sessionId, dataset, capturedAt, captureRevision>=1 and improvedRevision>=0<=captureRevision; optional improvedAt and improveLease={token, expiresAt}.
Reject a session filename that is not a safe basename ending .json.
Require a nonempty trimmed token; reject an unsafe ledger filename.
markDreamImproved locks then rereads the file.
Unreadable dream directory returns[].
Create a sibling temporary path by appending .<randomUUID>.tmp, write full UTF-8 content with mode 0600, chmod the temporary file 0600, then rename it over the target.
createIceCogneeExtension accepts optional storageDir/env/apiKey/fetch/now for embedding/tests.
storeEntry checks client/session and shuttingDown, snapshots client, sessionId and dataset, creates a request ID and start time, and emits a started observation.
probeHealth GETs <baseUrl without trailing slash>/health with optional x-api-key and AbortSignal.timeout(3000).
The per-prompt hook adds bounded recalled memory and any pending compaction context to one transient system prompt.
On tool_result ensure loaded, then require enabled, captureSession, captureTools, client and sessionId.
before_agent_start stores a redacted/truncated nonblank user prompt when session capture is enabled.
runImprove requires client/session/autoImprove, skips when improveInFlight and, for idle only, when now-lastImproveAt<300000 ms.
runDream requires client, autoImprove, no dreamInFlight and not shuttingDown.
Blackhole activity is inferred solely from <agentDir>/ice-blackhole/ice-blackhole-config.json: nonnull object, compaction not off, and compactionEngine blackhole or absent.
shouldOwnCompactionSummary is true only for own; auto always defers, regardless of Blackhole activity.
On session_compact ensure loaded; return when disabled or summary.trim empty.
On session_shutdown set shuttingDown=true and clear activity timer.
Register the exact descriptor/schema below.
Register /cognee once, ensure loaded, trim the argument string and split on whitespace into command/value/rest.
registerSettings namespace cognee provides enabled, autoRecall, autoRemember, compactionSummaryMode, checkpointRecall, captureSession, captureTools and autoImprove, in that order.
resources_discover unconditionally returns skillPaths:[getCogneeSkillsDir()], without ensureLoaded or enabled gate.
The extension observe helper makes a UUID, ISO actual-clock timestamp, current session/dataset/server model and optional request/status/duration metadata.
subscribeCogneeObservations inserts a callback into the global Set and returns deletion closure; no initial replay or directory filter.
updateStatusLine catches all UI access errors and does nothing without a usable UI/setStatus.
session_start awaits only ensureLoaded, resolves $project using ctx.cwd, applies search-tool state and binds host/Cognee IDs.
/cognee search requires a nonempty trimmed remainder; otherwise usage.
/cognee remember on/off with no additional token toggles automatic checkpoint remembering instead.
/cognee improve or improve now requires a client and session, not enabled or autoImprove.

on/off changes enabled; recall changes autoRecall; capture changes captureSession; tools changes captureTools; improve on/off changes autoImprove only with no rest; remember on/off changes autoRemember to compaction/off only with no rest; compact accepts auto/defer/own.
Empty /cognee or status awaits collectDoctor and notifies the exact detailed status string, then refreshes status UI.
/cognee flush, flush pending and flush uncertain are accepted; extra trailing tokens are ignored.
The package is private, ESM, version 0.4.3-ice.1, main index.ts, published-file selection index.ts/src/LICENSE/PROVENANCE.md, and ice.extensions=["./index.ts"].
Resolve directory from trimmed ICE_CODING_AGENT_DIR when nonempty, otherwise getAgentDir(); append ice-blackhole/ice-blackhole-config.json.
Start from validated file values.
saveConfig first calls loadConfig, including environment overlays, then shallow-merges the patch.
Load one closure-held effective config at registration.
Trim and split whitespace with a two-token limit; ignore extra tokens.
For each input message assign sourceIndex equal to its zero-based array position, not a durable session entry ID.
Apply replacements in the exact order below: CRLF to LF, remaining CR to LF, matching CSI-style escape sequences, then specified C0 controls.
